subject: geography
title: Earthquakes: Shaking the Ground
welcome_lead: Feel the ground tremble! Today you'll learn how earthquakes happen, how they are measured, and why some shake more than others.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on earthquakes, the Richter scale, focus and epicentre.
final_note: Excellent! You can now describe how earthquakes are measured and located.

concepts.def: Sudden shaking of Earth's crust from plate movement.
Point underground where the quake starts.
Point on surface directly above the focus.
Smaller quake following the main one.

walkthroughs.body_html: When plates push or grind, pressure builds in the rocks. Eventually they snap, releasing energy as seismic waves.
The focus is the underground starting point. The epicentre is the point on the surface directly above it, where shaking is usually strongest.
The Richter scale measures magnitude. Each step up means about 10 times more shaking. A 7.0 is far stronger than a 5.0!

options: The surface point above the focus
The deepest point in the ocean
